10. Externalities and Public Goods

Two scenes of market failure — externalities, where harm to others goes unpriced, and public goods, which everyone uses but no one buys.

  • Externalities and the Pigouvian Tax — Private marginal cost MPCMPCMPC sits below social marginal cost MSCMSCMSC — that gap is the externality. The market overproduces up to QpQ_pQp​, and welfare equal to the red triangle vanishes. Flip the Pigouvian tax τ=MD(Qs)\tau = MD(Q_s)τ=MD(Qs​) switch and the dashed cost curve aims exactly at the social optimum.
  • Public Goods and Free-Riding — Public-good demands sum vertically, not horizontally — everyone consumes the same unit at once. The Samuelson optimum is where the vertical sum meets marginal cost, but in the voluntary-contribution Nash equilibrium the weaker-demand side free-rides and supply falls short.
